headline: A CREATOR SPENT THREE YEARS AND ABOUT 50 ATTEMPTS PUBLICLY HUNTING A COPY OF A DISCONTINUED TOM FORD EYESHADOW, TOM FORD NEVER ANSWERED HER, AND THE RIVAL THAT DID SOLD OUT AT SEPHORA IN 12 HOURS AND LIFTED SALES OF ITS OTHER SHADES BY 305 PERCENT
deck: Hannah Chody was not pitching anybody.  She was documenting a search for 288,000 followers, and in doing so she ran three years of free product development in public.  Saie read it as a brief, flew her to Italy, and shipped the thing.
tldr: A creator spent three years and about 50 attempts publicly hunting a replacement for a discontinued Tom Ford eyeshadow, Tom Ford never replied, and the rival that flew her to Italy to develop it sold out at Sephora in 12 hours, took 7,500 waitlist sign-ups and saw a 305 percent sales lift across its other shades.  All figures are the brand's own.  Spend an afternoon searching your category for the words dupe, discontinued and bring back, and contact the best creator running that search with a product question rather than a campaign brief.

System1 told Waitrose last December that the one-minute cut of its 2025 Christmas film scored almost as well as the four-minute version, so Waitrose made this year's six minutes long, and this morning it sits twelfth of twelve on System1's first 2026 leaderboard at 5.6 stars against a maximum of 5.9 last year.  Read past the headline score on your own creative tests to the sentence explaining what drove it, put that driver at the top of your next brief, and test a cut-down before you commit production money to runtime.

Netflix funded eight seasons of Somebody Feed Phil; season nine will be free on YouTube with United Airlines as title sponsor, paying partly in crew and equipment so the production avoids landing with tons of kit in foreign countries.  Write down what your company physically owns that a production would otherwise rent or ship, and price that in-kind contribution as part of your next sponsorship deal rather than as a favour.

A study of 1,755 posts across 20 campaigns found paid-for creator posts average 334,055 views against 48,008 for gifted ones, and attributes the gap mostly to paid media budgets rather than better content, while styled shots beat product demonstrations 707,646 to 250,764 on views.  Report organic and paid creator reach as separate lines from now on, and brief one styled piece built to travel plus one demonstration built to convert, each with its own target.

TikTok is now charging more than a million of its best United States shoppers 9.99 dollars a month for free shipping, instant refunds and coupon bundles, against Amazon Prime at 14.99, while Mattel has just opened its first TikTok storefront with 20 products.  Audit your TikTok Shop listing this month so your best sellers carry the Plus shipping badge before Black Friday, and add shoppable links to your two best creator videos.

Billboard is putting YouTube data back into the United States charts from January and repricing a free ad-supported play from 40 percent of a paid stream to about 67 percent.  If you work with artists or labels, reopen any release plan landing after 16 January, push for a YouTube-first asset, and get the new chart weighting written into how the release is measured.

A games convention peaked at 514,200 concurrent viewers, about five and a half Wembleys at once, and the Twitch category around it recorded more hours watched than the event itself through restreams.  Ask every live partner for peak concurrents, average concurrents and total airtime before you sign, judge the audience on average concurrents, and stop accepting hours watched as a standalone number.
